intro: Here in Adıyaman province, the Adıyaman Museum opened its doors in 1982. It shows the finds of Mount Nemrut and Arsameia, alongside mosaics rescued from the towns that went under the waters of the Atatürk dam.
history: When it opened in 1982, the museum became the central collection for the kingdom of Commagene. In the 1980s, rescue excavations were run at settlements about to disappear under the Atatürk dam, and their finds were brought here too. That is how the mosaics of Samosata survive.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Commagenian works and the mosaics from Samosata. Then look for the finds from Nemrut and the material from the Perre necropolis.
facts: Did you know? Samosata was the Commagenian capital, and today it lies entirely beneath the reservoir. What is left of the city is the mosaics in this museum and a few crates of finds. Part of the collection comes from rescue excavations run before the reservoir waters rose.
outro: Our time in the Adıyaman Museum ends here. One small request before you go: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these pieces stay safe for the visitors who follow you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
